title: Selecting one trait unconsciously modifies other correlated parts

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Selecting one trait unconsciously modifies other correlated parts

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Because of laws of correlation of growth, when man selects for and augments any peculiarity, he almost certainly also modifies other parts of the structure without intending to.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Hence, if man goes on selecting, and thus augmenting, any peculiarity, he will almost certainly unconsciously modify other parts of the structure, owing to the mysterious laws of the correlation of growth.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter I, “Variation under Domestication”; section “Correlation of Growth”. Scope: domesticated animals and cultivated plants under artificial selection

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch01-05: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.76

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Multi-trait pedigrees, genomic associations and selection experiments directly measure correlated response. Public livestock and crop data provide enough breadth for a strong present-day test, though not every selection regime.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Estimate genetic correlations and correlated responses between deliberately selected traits and unselected traits in breeding populations. Nonzero repeatable correlated responses support the claim; consistently independent traits would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The phrase 'almost certainly' requires broad sampling.

Linkage can mimic pleiotropic correlation.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.84
data adequacy: 0.61
analysis feasibility: 0.78
discriminating power: 0.72
data existence: 0.83

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Correlated response is a standard variable, and pleiotropy catalogues plus multi-trait crop descriptors already show that selected changes often travel with other characters in major domestic species. Those sources are a subset of domesticated animals and plants, and turning them into a fair test of 'almost certainly' means months of harmonizing breeding studies. The null of independent modification is discriminable where multi-trait data exist.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Estimate genetic correlations, or correlated responses, between a selected target trait and traits that were not selection criteria, across breeding populations and crop evaluation trials. Widespread non-zero correlated change would support the expectation; a regular pattern of target traits changing alone would refute the 'almost certainly' clause.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Mendelian pleiotropy over-represents genes of large effect relative to the slight variations Darwin emphasized.

Genetic-correlation matrices are published study by study rather than in one livestock-and-crop archive.

Unintentional change can also come from drift and linkage, which mimic correlation of growth.

analysis feasibility: 0.52
